checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add deterministic WAV peak normalization

impact_assessment.why: Rendered and joined WAVs can be too quiet; a local normalization step makes levels usable without external audio tools.
impact_assessment.benefits: normalize scales a Coda WAV to a chosen peak with deterministic clamping and is idempotent, so it can be re-run safely.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: non-WAV or silent input must be handled without divide-by-zero or panic; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure normalize module with exact peak, idempotence and silence tests, a CLI command, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 113 tests green; normalization peak, idempotence and silence handling pinned by byte tests
Task 'coda-normalize' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add built-in score templates

impact_assessment.why: A blank score is a slow starting point; named templates give composers a deterministic sketch to render, vary or edit.
impact_assessment.benefits: templates lists the sketches and template <name> materializes one as canonical source, reusing the parser and serializer.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: every template must parse and re-serialize exactly; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Store templates as parseable source strings with a lookup API, add exact-list and round-trip tests, a CLI command, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 117 tests green; template listing exact and every template parses, renders and re-serializes identically

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add linear fade-in/fade-out to rendering

impact_assessment.why: Rendered pieces start and stop abruptly; fades are a basic mixing control needed to make sections and joins usable.
impact_assessment.benefits: --fade-in and --fade-out apply a deterministic linear envelope to both channels before WAV encoding, with zero values leaving existing renders unchanged.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: zero fades must be byte-identical to current golden vectors; fade lengths longer than the piece must clamp; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure fade module with exact frame-level tests, wire two CLI options into the audio path only, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 122 tests green; fades change audio edges with zero-fade digest equality to golden vectors
Task 'coda-fades' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add a deterministic echo/delay audio effect

impact_assessment.why: Rendered sounds are dry; a simple feedback delay adds a common mixing tool without external processors.
impact_assessment.benefits: --echo-delay and --echo-feedback add a bounded, reproducible comb echo to any render, seed, album track or joined section.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: zero delay must be byte-identical to current golden vectors; feedback must stay below 1 to avoid runaway gain; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure echo module with impulse-response and identity byte tests, wire two CLI options into the shared audio helper, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add a time-reversal score transform

impact_assessment.why: Reversal is a basic compositional device that turns an existing phrase into a new one without writing notes by hand.
impact_assessment.benefits: reverse mirrors every note's start around the score's end while preserving duration, pitch, velocity, pan and envelopes; applying it twice is an exact identity.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: note order and all non-start fields must be untouched so double reversal is byte-identical; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure reverse module with field-preservation and double-identity tests, a CLI command writing canonical source, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 132 tests green; double reversal is byte-identical in source and audio
Task 'coda-reverse' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add deterministic auto-pan

impact_assessment.why: Stereo output exists but the image is static unless every note sets its own pan; an LFO sweep gives motion without editing scores.
impact_assessment.benefits: --autopan-rate and --autopan-depth apply an equal-power stereo sweep to any render, with depth 0 preserving existing bytes.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: depth 0 must be byte-identical to golden vectors; gains must stay bounded; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure autopan module with identity, LFO-phase and bounded-gain tests, wire two CLI options into the shared audio helper, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.
